question: Northern Greece has been experiencing drought conditions for four consecutive years, which has resulted in a dramatic decline in agricultural production. Olives and other key crops has been particularly affected: yields are up to 50 % lower than the averages of the previous decade, leading thousands of small and medium-sized farms to an economic impasse.

For all its announcements, the Greek Government has failed to implement irrigation projects, dams or water storage programmes, leaving local communities unprotected. At the same time, the EU limits itself to general guidelines, without activating specific support tools for regions repeatedly affected by drought.

This situation undermines agricultural production, threatens food security and leads to rural depopulation. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: Does it intend to propose a specific drought adaptation programme in order to protect Greek (and at the same time European) production and, as a result, safeguard food self-sufficiency?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.12.2025) The Commission shares the concerns over water scarcity, especially in regions most acutely affected. As outlined in the Vision for Agriculture and Food1, a steady and safe water supply is key for future-proofing the agri-food sector.

The European Water Resilience Strategy2 reiterates that access to clean, affordable water is a human right, while recognising the need to curb demand and over-abstractions and to improve water efficiency and reuse to avoid supply disruptions.

The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)3 supports Member States with a range of tools, including investments, for efficient irrigation and climate adaptation measures, with the Greek CAP Strategic Plan 2023-20274 allocating EUR 1.4 billion for environmental and climate objectives including contributing to water savings and improving infrastructure5.
Day-to-day management of CAP-financed investments, including water infrastructure projects, falls under the responsibility of national authorities.

The CAP proposal for the period 2028-20346 requires Member States to continue to support farmers for climate change adaptation, water resilience and soil health, with tools such as investments in more efficient irrigation, water reuse and storage, rainwater harvesting and digital tools.

The latest update7 of Greece’s Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP)8, continues to support irrigation network infrastructure, while Cohesion Policy9 supports Member States to improve public water infrastructure. In addition, Horizon Europe10,11 financially supports research and innovation for water resilience in agriculture12.
1 Communication from the European Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European

Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions, A Vision for Agriculture and Food Shaping together an attractive farming and agri-food sector for future generations, COM/2025/75 final. 2 https://commission.europa.eu/topics/environment/water-resilience-strategy_en. 3 https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/common-agricultural-policy_en. 4 Union contribution for interventions P3-73-1.1 and P3-73-1.
